question.problem:
Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $p=⟨1,0,5⟩$, $q=⟨3,2,6⟩$, and $r=⟨0,4,1⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 6 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|+5\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(2\cdot 1-6\cdot 4)+0+5(3\cdot 4-2\cdot 0) \\  & =-22+60 \\  & =38\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|38|=38.
$$
